question.problem:
Using the standard form of the Maclaurin series of $\ln(1+x)$, find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion of the definite integral

$$
\displaystyle{\int_0^{1/2}\ln(1-x^2)\text{d}x}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
The power series expansion of $\ln(1+x)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1+x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Replacing $x$ with $-x^2$ in the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-{x}^{2}) & =(-{x}^{2})-\frac{1}{2}(-{x}^{2})^{2}+\frac{1}{3}(-{x}^{2})^{3}+⋯ \\  & =-{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{6}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-{x}^{2})\text{d}x & =\int (-{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{6}+⋯)\text{d}x \\  & =(-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{{x}^{5}}{5}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{{x}^{7}}{7}+⋯){|}_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\cdot {2}^{3}}-\frac{1}{2\cdot 5\cdot {2}^{5}}-\frac{1}{3\cdot 7\cdot {2}^{7}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{24}-\frac{1}{320}-\frac{1}{2688}+⋯\,\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We can get a numerical approximation by evaluating the first three terms. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-{x}^{2})\text{d}x & ≈-\frac{1}{24}-\frac{1}{320}-\frac{1}{2688}=-0.04516\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to five decimal places.

The exact value of the integral, rounded to five decimal places, is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-{x}^{2})\text{d}x & =-0.04523\,.\end{aligned}
$$

So, our estimation was pretty good!
